findings:
Declared and left, from the implementer's own deviations: the new refusal does not look through a quote or a list inside the typed block and is restricted to a block a fence closes, so two neighbours of the architect's shape stay as they read at the fork point - indented code inside a nested list in the typed block (`- a
  :::callout{...}
  - x
        code
       
  :::
`) and an unclosed typed block whose code ends the document (`- a
  :::callout{...}
      code
     
`). I measured both: DIVERGENT at the base 08c2e8ad and DIVERGENT at this head, Go reading the item tight where the engine reads it spread. Neither is a regression and neither is in the 916's classes; they belong to the whitespace-after-indented-code family the spec leaves to INFRA-719. The architect decides whether they stay declared or move.

The `<!a>` class (a lower-case declaration) is the only reading difference left in 13,780 html and indentation documents: an inline html node to the engine, text to Go. Its root cause predates this change and is not block HTML - `x <!a> y` parts the same way at the fork point - so it is goldmark's CommonMark 0.30 declaration rule against micromark's 0.31. The renderer escapes it (`\<!a>`) wherever it writes one, so no write of this change stores the shape. Reported in rounds 1 and 2, unchanged.
